title: Replace the DFlash2 candidate-lattice path selector with a fused walk
reasons: veto: most favourable defensible speedup 1.0051x < veto line 1.15x
measurement band is parametric, n=1, source=private archive p0-2026-11-13#section-3
claim capped by accounting: claimed 5.8900 ms > allowed 0.1107 ms (bytes 0.0003 / time 0.1107)
hypothesis: The selector reads as a hot spot in the draft path, so fusing hidden projection + edge scoring + path walk into one kernel yields a measurable end-to-end gain on the c1 short-context decode cycle.

mechanism.name: fuse hidden projection + edge scoring + path walk into one selector kernel
mechanism.justification: The selector is latency-bound, not byte-bound: its entire unfused cost is 110.7 us/step (hidden proj 14.1 + scoring 82.0 + walk 14.6), so even deleting it completely can only save 0.11 ms of a 22.68 ms cycle. The byte ledger caps the claim at 0.0003 ms, far below the time accounting, so the time accounting binds - and it is 0.49 % of the cycle.
